Job Description

Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Strategic Philanthropy (SVP) at the Hoag Hospital Foundation (HHF), the Executive Director of Campaigns (ED) is responsible for leading the planning and execution of major philanthropic campaigns, including the upcoming comprehensive campaign. In partnership with senior HHF leadership, the ED will collaborate across the foundation and hospital to establish campaign priorities, strategies, policies, timelines, and operations. This role ensures alignment across all aspects of each campaign, refining goals and approaches as needed to achieve ambitious philanthropic objectives.

Responsibilities

Key responsibilities include oversight of all campaign-related activities from planning through the public phase and post-campaign assessment and stewardship.

Oversee feasibility studies and translate findings into actionable plans
Partner with clinical and hospital leadership to identify and articulate campaign priorities
Develop timelines, case statements, naming opportunities, budgets, volunteer structures, branding, and messaging
Create and manage day-to-day implementation of the campaign workplan
Convene and engage HHF staff to ensure alignment with campaign goals
Provide training to HHF staff, hospital and clinical partners, and board members as appropriate about campaigns
Monitor, track, and report on campaign progress and outcomes
Facilitate the transition from one campaign phase to the next
Serve as the liaison and provide oversight to any external campaign consultants
Partner with colleagues across HHF to provide relevant donor engagement opportunities, execute campaign messaging, report on milestones and impacts, and create meaningful recognition touchpoints and events

This role requires a strategic, collaborative leader who can inspire cross-organizational engagement, ensure disciplined execution, and steward a transformative campaign effort for Hoag.

Bachelor’s degree required .
Expertise and depth of understanding of best practices and trends in comprehensive and capital campaigns

The ability to adapt to and lead through changing circumstances in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
A creative approach to problem-solving coupled with strong critical-thinking and analytical skills.
Strong communication and organizational skills .

jobs.description:
Citi is establishing a new, unified firmwide AI organisation under a newly created Group Head of Artificial Intelligence — merging the firm's Head of AI and CTO responsibilities into a single executive accountable for AI-led transformation across every business and function. This post-merger structure is intentionally distinct from prior models and will be the engine through which Citi competes in the AI era.

The COO for Group AI is the operational backbone of this new organization. As a critical partner to the Group Head of AI, this leader will drive strategic execution, own the operating model, hold the budget and ROI narrative, and partner with HR on the most consequential workforce transformation in the firm's recent history. This is a rare C-16 mandate to stand up - and run - the operating engine of one of the most consequential transformations in global financial services.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Business Execution
Partner with the Group Head of AI and the pillar leads to establish actionable team wide operating plans, OKRs, and KPIs for the Group AI organization.
Drive end-to-end program execution across all seven AI pillars - from AI Strategy and Responsible AI through to the Core Platform, Agent Factory, and AI-First Development - ensuring delivery on time, within budget, and to required quality standards.
Own the OM/AI workstream: design, refine, and continuously evolve the operating model for the new Group AI organization, including governance forums, decision rights, and cross-pillar coordination.
Identify opportunities for process improvement and operational efficiencies across the AI development, deployment, and adoption lifecycle.
Financial Management & ROI Ownership
Act as end-to-end owner of the Group AI budget and investment portfolio, in close partnership with Finance.
Lead firm-wide AI ROI forecasting, financial benefits realisation, and quantified business case discipline across all pillars.
Set financial targets, manage expense productivity, own the approval process for hiring and discretionary spend, and review monthly financials with the Group Head of AI to identify variances and corrective actions.
Ensure efficient utilisation of AI infrastructure, compute, data, and vendor spend at global scale.
Workforce Transformation & Talent
Partner with HR to lead the workforce transformation agenda for the firm - including workforce impact modelling, reskilling, talent strategy, and organizational change required for an AI-first Citi.
Lead the Group AI workforce management council and associated deliverables; own headcount planning, location strategy, and talent mobility within the Group AI organization.
Champion a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and ownership across a global team operating in a regulated environment.
Governance, Performance & Reporting
Act as Chief of Staff to the Group Head of AI: run executive governance forums, leadership offsites, and cadence with the Board, regulators, and the Operating Committee.
Provide central oversight of business-critical OKRs, milestone reporting, and executive dashboards to monitor the health of the AI portfolio.
Establish and manage a robust governance framework for the tracking and realisation of strategic AI initiatives.
Stakeholder Management
Serve as the primary operating interface to the COO function, the Head of Tech & Business Enablement, Finance, HR, Risk, Legal, and the business-line COOs.
Cultivate trusted, credible relationships with senior leaders across the firm; communicate progress, challenges, and successes to diverse audiences with tailored messaging.

What Success Looks Like (First 12 Months)

A single, transparent AI portfolio view with clear ROI commitments by pillar and business line, agreed with Finance.
A working operating rhythm (planning, governance, reporting) trusted by the Group Head of AI, the CFO, and the CHRO.
A workforce transformation roadmap co-owned with HR and adopted across the firm.
Demonstrable acceleration in AI program delivery velocity - without compromising controls.

Qualifications

15+ years of progressive leadership experience in Financial Services, including a senior COO, Chief of Staff, or Business Execution role driving strategy, transformation, or large-scale operational change in a regulated environment.
Seasoned operator with proven success running Citi-scale, highly-matrixed transformation programs; able to set priorities and triage in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
Strong financial acumen - credible partner to the CFO; demonstrated experience owning multi-hundred-million-dollar investment portfolios, P&L management, budgeting, and ROI realisation.
Workforce and talent fluency - credible partner to the CHRO; track record on workforce transformation, talent strategy, and change management at scale.
Disciplined execution and operational excellence — process-oriented, with experience applying structured methodologies to complex transformations.
Technology and AI acumen - fluency in modern AI sufficient to challenge, prioritise, and translate; track record of partnering on technology-led transformation. Deep technical expertise is not required, but genuine curiosity and conviction are.
Risk & Compliance awareness - comprehensive understanding of corporate governance, regulatory frameworks, and risk management in global banking.
Influence & communication - excellent communication and interpersonal skills; able to influence at Board, regulator, and Operating Committee level.
Low-ego integrator - the kind of leader whose presence quietly elevates every other executive in the room; bias to action; resilient under pressure.
Education
Bachelor's degree required, preferably in business, finance, or a related field.
MBA or other advanced degree strongly preferred.

Why This Role

You will be the operating partner to the Group Head of AI at the moment Citi reorganizes itself around artificial intelligence. The decisions you make in the first year - on operating model, on capital allocation, on workforce - will define how the firm competes for the next decade

Company Description
The Johnny Appleseed Educational Center and Museum celebrates the life and legacy of John Chapman, known as Johnny Appleseed, and the values of generosity, humility, stewardship, thrift, entrepreneurship, and care for others. Visitors encounter unique artifacts such as the Dock Family Bible, believed to have been carried by Johnny Appleseed and preserved by his descendants since 1849. The museum grounds feature a Memorial Orchard with trees descended from those Johnny planted, as well as a Children’s Garden that provides space for families to play, picnic, and take photos. The Executive Director is a full-time, on-site leadership role based in Urbana, OH, responsible for overseeing all aspects of the museum’s operations and strategic direction. This position manages staff and volunteers, ensures high-quality visitor experiences, and maintains the museum’s collections, exhibits, and grounds. The Executive Director develops and implements educational programs, community outreach initiatives, and partnerships that advance the museum’s mission and visibility. Daily responsibilities include budgeting and financial oversight, fundraising and donor relations, grant writing, and reporting to the board. The role also involves setting organizational goals, monitoring performance, ensuring compliance with relevant regulations, and fostering a collaborative, inclusive workplace culture aligned with Johnny Appleseed’s values.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Catalyze479 Fund
jobs.description:
As Deputy Director, Catalyze479 Fund, at Renaissance Philanthropy, you will play a key role in helping build and execute the Catalyze479 Fund in Northwest Arkansas. This is a rare opportunity to help source and diligence investments, support portfolio companies, strengthen local ecosystem relationships, and contribute to the growth of a philanthropic investment fund focused on early-stage companies and community-embedded businesses. The ideal candidate is someone who is equal parts investor, relationship builder, and operator.

This position is based Northwest Arkansas (within 30 miles of Bentonville) — on-site required. At least 2-3 days of in-office time is required per week.

Compensation

$135,000–$150,000 base salary range, plus a comprehensive benefits package, 401(k) contribution match, $550 / month in additional fringe benefits, unlimited PTO, and performance-based bonus. This role does not come with carried interest, given the investments are coming from a philanthropic fund.

Reports To:

Director, Catalyze479 Fund

Employment Type:

Full-time

About the Catalyze479 Strategy of the Northwest Arkansas Innovation Fund

Northwest Arkansas (NWA) is one of America’s most dynamic and fast-growing regions — home to Fortune 500 firms Walmart, Tyson Foods, and JB Hunt; an extraordinary outdoor lifestyle that includes one of the top mountain bike networks in the world; and an emerging startup ecosystem.

With support from the Walton Family Foundation, Renaissance Philanthropy has launched the Catalyze479 Fund to bridge the earliest stage capital gap for Northwest Arkansas-based enterprises. This revolving, nonprofit philanthropic fund will provide capital to validation-stage companies at the most critical stages of development and help prime these companies to grow, create high-quality local jobs, and receive future private sector angel and venture capital. Any return from the investments will be re-invested into the Fund to sustain future investments with the same parameters (Northwest Arkansas-based companies).

The Fund will invest via two main strategies, with a maximum initial check size of $500,000:

A Venture Validation strategy targeting idea-stage through validation-stage / pre-seed companies in Northwest Arkansas that are building scalable, technology-forward businesses that are too early-stage or high-risk for traditional venture capital investment. These companies should have the potential to create positive change, diversify the economic base of Northwest Arkansas, and generate high-quality local jobs.
A Main Street strategy investing in scalable community-embedded businesses—the bookstores, restaurants, and neighborhood anchors that provide local character and jobs.

Our goal is to deploy capital across both fund strategies, build a portfolio of companies generating follow-on investment, create quality jobs in the region, and become part of the connective tissue of a robust, inclusive, and ambitious startup community.

The fund’s theory of change is that place-based equity investment from a philanthropic fund paired with deep founder support and a robust ecosystem of co-investors and community partners can diversify NWA’s economy, create quality jobs for Arkansans, and ultimately improve the local community.

Catalyze479 will deploy capital as Mission-Related Investments (MRIs). Financial return and mission impact are both objectives.

The Role

Renaissance Philanthropy is seeking a Deputy Director for Catalyze479 — someone who is equal parts investor, relationship builder, and operator. This is a rare opportunity to help build and scale an early-stage philanthropic investment fund by supporting sourcing, due diligence, portfolio management, ecosystem engagement, and fund operations across two distinct strategies.

You will be a senior local member of the Catalyze479 team, working directly with the Fund Director to help execute the fund’s strategy, build trusted relationships across Northwest Arkansas, and ensure strong investment and portfolio management processes. You will operate with meaningful responsibility while partnering closely with the Director on priorities, external positioning, and fund-level decisions.

If the fund is successful in its first 30 months, Catalyze479 will have deployed capital across both fund strategies, built a portfolio of companies generating follow-on investment, supported quality job creation in the region, and established the NWA Innovation Fund as an important part of a more robust, inclusive, and ambitious startup community in Northwest Arkansas. As Deputy Director, you will play a central role in helping achieve those outcomes.

Core Responsibilities

Fund Build-Out & Investment Strategy

Support the Fund Director in refining the fund’s investment thesis, criteria, and operating model in partnership with Renaissance Philanthropy leadership and stakeholders

Help define, track, and communicate the fund’s theory of impact — how equity investment translates to regional economic development, job creation, and founder success

Ensure all fund activities comply with Renaissance Philanthropy's Investment Policy, Conflict of Interest Policy, and applicable IRS requirements governing mission-related investments by 501(c)(3) organizations, including documentation standards for mission nexus at the time of each investment

Sourcing, Due Diligence & Portfolio Management

Build and support an active deal pipeline across both fund strategies — Venture Validation and Main Street

Support end-to-end investment processes, including sourcing, founder assessment, due diligence, investment memo creation, Investment Committee preparation, and coordination with the Fund Director on investment recommendations and terms

Work closely with portfolio founders post-investment as a thought partner, advisor, and connector — helping them access follow-on capital, key hires, and customers

Track and report on both financial performance and community impact metrics, including jobs created, capital leverage, and founder outcome

Ecosystem Building & External Relations

Represent Catalyze479 at regional events, founder and investor convenings, and community gatherings

Cultivate deep relationships with regional anchors (Walmart, Tyson, JB Hunt, and others), universities, economic development organizations, and civic leaders

Build co-investment pipelines with national and regional VC firms, angel networks, and philanthropic partners

Identify and engage complementary ecosystem players — understanding where to partner, where to lead, and how to build collective momentum toward a more inclusive and dynamic startup community in NWA

Fundraising & Stakeholder Reporting

Contribute to regular reporting on fund performance, portfolio developments, and strategic priorities, including drafting updates, preparing materials, and synthesizing portfolio and impact data for the Fund Director and Renaissance Philanthropy leadership

Identify and cultivate additional philanthropic and impact investors to invest in the

companies in the portfolio to grow the portfolio’s investor base over time

Develop compelling, data-driven impact narratives that demonstrate the fund’s value to the region

Team & Operations

Support onboarding, coordination, and day-to-day collaboration with future Catalyze479 team members, interns, contractors, or shared-service partners as the fund grows

Build internal systems and operational processes that allow the fund to scale, with support from Renaissance Philanthropy’s shared services

Leverage AI tools in day-to-day operations — from deal sourcing and due diligence to communications and reporting

Qualifications

The ideal candidate is a builder with a genuine love for startups, people, and community. You understand the mechanics of early-stage businesses across very different environments — from venture-backed tech to main street retail — and you have the judgment to recognize exceptional founders and differentiated ideas. You are a hyper-connector who forges relationships that outlast your involvement, and you are energized, not paralyzed, by the opportunity to design something new.

Required:

5–8+ years of experience in venture capital, early-stage investing, startup operations, entrepreneurship, economic development, or related fields — ideally a combination
Track record of making or supporting equity investments, including sourcing, diligence, and portfolio management
Familiarity with pre-seed and seed-stage investment structures: cap table math, term sheets, and early-stage KPIs
Demonstrated ability to mentor and advise founders, both pre- and post-investment
Experience building or launching new organizations, funds, or programs from scratch
Strong relationships in the startup and investor community, with the ability to attract co-investors and credible deal flow
Deep commitment to Northwest Arkansas — through existing roots in the region or a genuine, specific enthusiasm for relocating and embedding in the community
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex investment themes for diverse audiences
AI-enabled: you actively use AI tools in your work

Preferred:

Existing networks in NWA or the broader Arkansas and Midwest startup ecosystem
Experience collaborating with early-career investment professionals, analysts, interns, or cross-functional partners
Comfort with quantitative analytics, including Excel modeling and financial analysis

Values

You Will Thrive Within Our Team If You:

You believe in the power of entrepreneurship and innovation to create economic opportunity — and you see NWA as one of the most exciting places in America to prove it. You have strong mission and vision alignment.
You can build from scratch, make decisions with incomplete information, and move mountains when you need to. You exhibit high agency.

You know that the best investments often come from the deepest relationships. You are a hyper-connector who gets to know everybody and understands who should meet whom. You value exceptional talent and the power of networks.
You are not afraid of ambiguity. You ask tons of questions. Intellectual curiosity is your default operating mode. You are comfortable working in fast-moving and ambitious environments.
You are as excited about being part of building Northwest Arkansas into a destination for entrepreneurs and young professionals as you are about deploying capital. You love building community.

jobs.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

At The Well is seeking an experienced Chief Development Officer (CDO) to serve as the organization’s senior executive leader for contributed revenue and philanthropic sustainability. Reporting to the CEO and partnering closely with the COO, the CDO will hold primary executive accountability for achieving At The Well’s annual contributed-revenue goals, building a strong culture of philanthropy, and developing a comprehensive, multi-year development strategy that supports organizational growth and long-term sustainability.

This is both a strategic and hands-on role, accountable for achieving and growing a seven-figure annual contributed-revenue goal. The CDO will personally cultivate and close major gifts; lead individual, institutional, and grassroots fundraising; equip the CEO and Board as fundraising partners; and build the team and infrastructure needed for success. We are seeking an expert fundraising leader with an entrepreneurial spirit—someone who is ready to build, bring new ideas to life, and create something exceptional and enduring for At The Well.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Fundraising leadership & strategy

Develop, own, and execute a comprehensive annual and multi-year fundraising strategy with clear revenue goals, action plans, timelines, and measures of success.
Build a diversified contributed-revenue model across major gifts, individual giving, institutional funding, grassroots and digital campaigns, and other appropriate channels.
Develop revenue forecasts, pipeline projections, metrics, and reporting that identify risks and opportunities, inform organizational budgeting, and provide the CEO, COO, and Board with clear analysis of fundraising performance.
Represent At The Well at select public events, donor gatherings, conferences, and speaking engagements.

Individual giving & major gifts

Personally build and manage a portfolio of major donors and prospects, developing and executing individualized qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for each relationship.
Identify, research, cultivate, solicit, and close major gifts, with demonstrated focus on developing a pipeline of future opportunities.
Serve as the principal strategist for At The Well’s highest-priority donor relationships, overseeing moves management and equipping the CEO and Board with prospect strategy, meeting preparation, introductions, cultivation plans, solicitation support, and timely follow-up.
Provide high-touch, donor-centered stewardship that deepens relationships, supports retention and upgrades, and connects donors meaningfully to At The Well’s mission and impact.
Lead prospect research and qualification, using iWave and other tools strategically to identify and prioritize new opportunities.
Develop and implement grassroots and digital fundraising strategies in partnership with marketing and communications staff, analyzing results and adapting approaches to strengthen acquisition, retention, and the major-donor pipeline.

Institutional giving & grants

Own At The Well’s institutional fundraising strategy and grants pipeline, including funder identification, relationship development, opportunity positioning, proposal priorities, renewals, reporting, and stewardship.
Manage a grant writer or other institutional-giving support, establishing priorities, timelines, standards, and accountability while retaining executive ownership of funder relationships and results.
Coordinate proposal and report development across the organization, personally shaping, editing, or drafting high-priority and time-sensitive materials when needed.

Development communications, events, & external relationships

Develop a deep understanding of At The Well’s work and lead the creation of compelling fundraising messaging and materials, including the case for support, proposals, decks, donor reports, and campaign collateral, in partnership with the marketing and communications team.
Lead all development communications efforts, including regular donor communications as well as special grassroots fundraising campaigns,
Design and oversee fundraising and cultivation events with clear relationship and revenue objectives, integrating philanthropy thoughtfully into community and programmatic experiences.
Develop strategic relationships with donors, foundations, Jewish communal leaders, philanthropic advisors, and partner organizations that expand At The Well’s reach and funding opportunities.

Team, systems, & development operations

Recruit, manage, mentor, and develop development staff and contractors, including a development associate to manage data and CRM as well as a contract grant writer. Establish clear roles, goals, accountability, and opportunities for growth with these individuals.
Own the strategy, standards, reporting requirements, and organizational accountability for Salesforce and related development systems, partnering across the organization to ensure strong data integrity, donor documentation, gift processing, acknowledgment, reporting, and workflows.
Oversee the development budget
and make disciplined recommendations about investments in staff, technology, research, events, consultants, and donor engagement.

Executive leadership

At The Well’s Chiefs are more than functional leaders; they share responsibility for the strength, sustainability, and long-term success of the organization. This role requires someone who can hold a strategic vision while remaining deeply engaged in the work required to bring it to life. The CEO, COO, and CDO will work as a closely aligned executive team, with each leader holding clear ownership of their area while collaborating across functions to advance the organization as a whole.
Hold primary executive accountability for At The Well’s contributed-revenue performance
while remaining willing to do the hands-on work required to achieve results. We are a small team that both strategizes and executes. 
Lead with initiative and an organization-wide perspective
, understanding how development connects to programs, operations, culture, finances, communications, and mission.
Partner closely with the CEO and COO
on organizational strategy, planning, resource allocation, risk management, culture, and At The Well’s long-term health.

HOW SUCCESS WILL BE MEASURED

The CDO’s performance will be assessed through both fundraising results and the long-term strength of the development function. Core measures will include:
Annual contributed revenue raised against goal and progress toward multi-year growth targets.
Strength, value, diversification, and movement of the donor and funder pipeline, including major-gift solicitations and gifts closed.
Donor acquisition, retention, renewal, reactivation, and upgrade results.
Institutional-giving outcomes and the accuracy and usefulness of revenue forecasts, dashboards, CRM records, and reporting.
Effectiveness of the CEO, Board, staff, systems, and development team as coordinated and sustainable fundraising resources.

QUALIFICATIONS

7+ years of progressively responsible nonprofit fundraising experience, including leadership of a comprehensive development function and experience operating as a senior organizational leader.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing successful annual and multi-year strategies across multiple contributed-revenue channels, with a track record of personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing multiple six-figure gifts; experience developing or closing seven-figure opportunities is strongly preferred.
Experience building and managing a qualified major-donor portfolio, using disciplined moves management, and partnering with a CEO, senior leaders, and Board members to advance donor relationships and build an organization-wide culture of philanthropy.
Strong financial literacy, including experience with revenue forecasting, pipeline analysis, budgeting, performance metrics, and reporting.
Demonstrated ability to build, manage, mentor, and develop staff and contractors while working entrepreneurially, setting priorities, taking initiative, and remaining willing to execute the work directly when needed.
Knowledge of the Jewish philanthropic landscape is strongly preferred. Established relationships with relevant donors, foundations, communal leaders, or philanthropic networks—particularly in the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles—are a significant advantage.
Commitment to At The Well’s mission and values, with strong written, verbal, listening, presentation, and relationship-building skills and the discretion required to manage confidential donor information.
Experience using Salesforce or a comparable fundraising CRM; experience with prospect-research tools such as iWave is preferred, along with the ability to learn new systems quickly.
Commitment to building and fostering a diverse, inclusive, and collegial workplace, with multicultural competence and the ability to work respectfully across lines of difference.

LOCATION & EMPLOYMENT TYPE

This is a full-time, virtual position based in California. Candidates in the San Francisco Bay Area or Los Angeles are strongly preferred because of At The Well’s growing relationships and fundraising opportunities in those regions.
The role requires regular in-person donor and community engagement in California and beyond, national travel, and occasional evening and weekend commitments.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

The salary range for this position is $175,000-200,000, commensurate with experience. 

At The Well provides a flexible time-off plan that aims to give you space and time away from the “office” to be a whole human, while also ensuring the work moves forward. ATW observes office closures in accordance with many Jewish and Federal holidays. Additional benefits include: 
Medical (base package costs are covered by ATW)

Retirement plan + 401(k) match 
Short- and long-term disability 
Professional development 
Work-from-home monthly stipend

jobs.description:
Working at Yale means contributing to a better tomorrow. Whether you are a current resident of our New Haven-based community, eligible for opportunities through the New Haven Hiring Initiative, or a newcomer, interested in exploring all that Yale has to offer, your talents and contributions are welcome. Discover your opportunities at Yale!

Overview

The Director of Development & Alumni Affairs reports to the Dean of David Geffen School of Drama/Yale Repertory Theatre (DGSD/YRT). Working closely with the DGSD/YRT Associate Dean/Managing Director, the Director leads and supervises the Development and Alumni Affairs Office, overseeing annual fundraising, alumni communications, and related organizational efforts and events that support a dynamic, mission-driven operation for DGSD/YRT.

The Director is instrumental in cultivating and sustaining meaningful relationships with DGSD/YRT alumni, donors, friends, and prospects; overseeing volunteer initiatives; and meeting annual fundraising goals while delivering exceptional stewardship experiences that deepen donor and alumni commitment. The role includes planning and executing monthly, quarterly, and annual messaging; producing program- and constituency-specific communications (including newsletters); and reporting on fundraising trends and opportunities. The position requires availability for occasional travel and evening/weekend events. It also includes mentoring DGSD students in professional work assignments in the Development Department and potentially teaching workshops/courses in DGSD’s Theater Management Program.

Essential Duties

Lead all fundraising strategy and execution for DGSD/YRT, aligning solicitation campaigns and alumni affairs priorities with school and university objectives.
Design, implement, and manage comprehensive fundraising programs, including annual giving, major gifts, endowment, planned giving, and capital campaigns, in partnership with DGSD/YRT leadership and the Yale University Development Office.
Direct the full donor/prospect lifecycle: identification, research, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, proposal development, closure, stewardship, and follow-up; oversee accurate tracking and monitoring of donors and prospects.
Set and manage measurable fundraising performance targets: revenue, participation, activity.
Monitor annual giving performance and solicitation strategies on a regular cadence; analyze participation and dollar trends, identify opportunities, and adjust strategies to meet goals.
Build and sustain strong alumni engagement and relationships; review donor profiles to identify and strategically solicit top annual donors.
Oversee the planning and delivery of alumni affairs programs and events, including targeted annual initiatives; plan and attend on- and off-campus meetings and events.
Prepare and/or oversee compelling gift and grant proposals, coordinate with the University Office of Corporate and Foundation Relations on proposals for specific projects.
Serve as primary liaison to the DGSD Board of Advisors, organizing Board meetings and overseeing Board committees, solicitations, and stewardship.
Serve as liaison to the Yale University Development Office and relevant university officers/departments; collaborate closely with faculty, staff, students, and campus partners on fundraising initiatives.
Develop and manage the Development/Alumni Affairs budget; ensure effective resource allocation in support of strategic goals.
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing development team; establish a culture of responsiveness, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Supervise and mentor student rotations within the Development Office; coordinate with the Chair of the Theater Management Program to implement and evaluate student development training.
Participate in annual and long-range planning processes; contribute to short- and long-term fundraising strategy development with senior management.
Travel as required to support donor engagement and fundraising activity, consistent with Yale fundraising expectations.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills And Abilities

Experience and proficiency in fundraising strategy, campaign planning, and execution (annual giving, major gifts, endowment, planned giving, capital campaigns) as well as prospect research, qualification/rating, portfolio management, and proposal/grant writing.
High level of integrity and ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion.
Well-developed written and oral communication skills. Excellent writing, proofreading, and editing skills; excellent attention to detail; ability to prioritize and balance multiple tasks and projects simultaneously; strong follow-through.
Demonstrable experience in alumni engagement and in program and event planning.
Ability to work effectively with the Dean, other senior members of the school, and the university's academic and administrative leadership. Excellent interpersonal skills in relation to donors, volunteers, students, and colleagues.

Preferred Skills And Abilities

Experience in or understanding of the performing arts or theater.
Experience working effectively within a complex academic environment.

. This position leads the organization's relationship-based fundraising efforts, cultivating and securing philanthropic support from major individual donors, private foundations, and corporate partners to advance the growth of agroforestry across the Midwest.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Advancement, the Director of Philanthropy serves as Savanna Institute's primary frontline fundraiser. The position develops and manages a portfolio of prospects, high-capacity donors, and institutional funders, builds trust-based philanthropic partnerships, and works collaboratively across the organization to align funding opportunities with strategic priorities.

We seek applicants who share our passion for ecological and equitable agriculture as a climate solution and who are motivated to widen the circle of people who have the opportunity to inform, support, and benefit from its development. To that end, we are seeking a diversity of voices at the table and strongly encourage people of color, women, LGBTQIA+ individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, foreign-born residents, and veterans to apply.

Hours:
full-time
Location:
Remote, located within one hour’s drive of Madison, WI or Spring Green, WI
Start Date:
November 2, 2026
Salary:
$75,000-$87,000, based on experience

Other duties as assigned by the Advancement Team

With support from the Walton Family Foundation, Renaissance Philanthropy has launched the Catalyze479 Fund to bridge the earliest stage capital gap for Northwest Arkansas-based enterprises. This revolving, nonprofit philanthropic fund will provide capital to validation-stage companies at the most critical stages of development and help prime these companies to grow, create high-quality local jobs, and receive future private sector angel and venture capital. Any return from the investments will be re-invested into the Fund to sustain future investments with the same parameters (Northwest Arkansas-based companies).

The Fund will invest via two main strategies, with a maximum initial check size of $500,000:

A Venture Validation strategy targeting idea-stage through validation-stage / pre-seed companies in Northwest Arkansas that are building scalable, technology-forward businesses that are too early-stage or high-risk for traditional venture capital investment. These companies should have the potential to create positive change, diversify the economic base of Northwest Arkansas, and generate high-quality local jobs.
A Main Street strategy investing in scalable community-embedded businesses—the bookstores, restaurants, and neighborhood anchors that provide local character and jobs.

Our goal is to deploy capital across both fund strategies, build a portfolio of companies generating follow-on investment, create quality jobs in the region, and become part of the connective tissue of a robust, inclusive, and ambitious startup community.

The fund’s theory of change is that place-based equity investment from a philanthropic fund paired with deep founder support and a robust ecosystem of co-investors and community partners can diversify NWA’s economy, create quality jobs for Arkansans, and ultimately improve the local community.

Catalyze479 will deploy capital as Mission-Related Investments (MRIs). Financial return and mission impact are both objectives.

The Role

Renaissance Philanthropy is seeking a Deputy Director for Catalyze479 — someone who is equal parts investor, relationship builder, and operator. This is a rare opportunity to help build and scale an early-stage philanthropic investment fund by supporting sourcing, due diligence, portfolio management, ecosystem engagement, and fund operations across two distinct strategies.

You will be a senior local member of the Catalyze479 team, working directly with the Fund Director to help execute the fund’s strategy, build trusted relationships across Northwest Arkansas, and ensure strong investment and portfolio management processes. You will operate with meaningful responsibility while partnering closely with the Director on priorities, external positioning, and fund-level decisions.

If the fund is successful in its first 30 months, Catalyze479 will have deployed capital across both fund strategies, built a portfolio of companies generating follow-on investment, supported quality job creation in the region, and established the NWA Innovation Fund as an important part of a more robust, inclusive, and ambitious startup community in Northwest Arkansas. As Deputy Director, you will play a central role in helping achieve those outcomes.

Core Responsibilities

Fund Build-Out & Investment Strategy

Support the Fund Director in refining the fund’s investment thesis, criteria, and operating model in partnership with Renaissance Philanthropy leadership and stakeholders

Help define, track, and communicate the fund’s theory of impact — how equity investment translates to regional economic development, job creation, and founder success

Ensure all fund activities comply with Renaissance Philanthropy's Investment Policy, Conflict of Interest Policy, and applicable IRS requirements governing mission-related investments by 501(c)(3) organizations, including documentation standards for mission nexus at the time of each investment

Sourcing, Due Diligence & Portfolio Management

Build and support an active deal pipeline across both fund strategies — Venture Validation and Main Street

Support end-to-end investment processes, including sourcing, founder assessment, due diligence, investment memo creation, Investment Committee preparation, and coordination with the Fund Director on investment recommendations and terms

Work closely with portfolio founders post-investment as a thought partner, advisor, and connector — helping them access follow-on capital, key hires, and customers

Track and report on both financial performance and community impact metrics, including jobs created, capital leverage, and founder outcome

Ecosystem Building & External Relations

Represent Catalyze479 at regional events, founder and investor convenings, and community gatherings

Cultivate deep relationships with regional anchors (Walmart, Tyson, JB Hunt, and others), universities, economic development organizations, and civic leaders

Build co-investment pipelines with national and regional VC firms, angel networks, and philanthropic partners

Identify and engage complementary ecosystem players — understanding where to partner, where to lead, and how to build collective momentum toward a more inclusive and dynamic startup community in NWA

Fundraising & Stakeholder Reporting

Contribute to regular reporting on fund performance, portfolio developments, and strategic priorities, including drafting updates, preparing materials, and synthesizing portfolio and impact data for the Fund Director and Renaissance Philanthropy leadership

Identify and cultivate additional philanthropic and impact investors to invest in the

companies in the portfolio to grow the portfolio’s investor base over time

Develop compelling, data-driven impact narratives that demonstrate the fund’s value to the region

Team & Operations

Support onboarding, coordination, and day-to-day collaboration with future Catalyze479 team members, interns, contractors, or shared-service partners as the fund grows

Build internal systems and operational processes that allow the fund to scale, with support from Renaissance Philanthropy’s shared services

Leverage AI tools in day-to-day operations — from deal sourcing and due diligence to communications and reporting

Qualifications

The ideal candidate is a builder with a genuine love for startups, people, and community. You understand the mechanics of early-stage businesses across very different environments — from venture-backed tech to main street retail — and you have the judgment to recognize exceptional founders and differentiated ideas. You are a hyper-connector who forges relationships that outlast your involvement, and you are energized, not paralyzed, by the opportunity to design something new.

Required:

5–8+ years of experience in venture capital, early-stage investing, startup operations, entrepreneurship, economic development, or related fields — ideally a combination
Track record of making or supporting equity investments, including sourcing, diligence, and portfolio management
Familiarity with pre-seed and seed-stage investment structures: cap table math, term sheets, and early-stage KPIs
Demonstrated ability to mentor and advise founders, both pre- and post-investment
Experience building or launching new organizations, funds, or programs from scratch
Strong relationships in the startup and investor community, with the ability to attract co-investors and credible deal flow
Deep commitment to Northwest Arkansas — through existing roots in the region or a genuine, specific enthusiasm for relocating and embedding in the community
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex investment themes for diverse audiences
AI-enabled: you actively use AI tools in your work

Preferred:

Existing networks in NWA or the broader Arkansas and Midwest startup ecosystem
Experience collaborating with early-career investment professionals, analysts, interns, or cross-functional partners
Comfort with quantitative analytics, including Excel modeling and financial analysis

Values

You Will Thrive Within Our Team If You:

You can recruit co-investors, win over founders, and bring skeptics along — because you are genuinely compelling and you care about the people around you. You inspire others and are highly collaborative.
You know that the best investments often come from the deepest relationships. You are a hyper-connector who gets to know everybody and understands who should meet whom. You value exceptional talent and the power of networks.
You are not afraid of ambiguity. You ask tons of questions. Intellectual curiosity is your default operating mode. You are comfortable working in fast-moving and ambitious environments.
You are as excited about being part of building Northwest Arkansas into a destination for entrepreneurs and young professionals as you are about deploying capital. You love building community.

This is both a strategic and hands-on role, accountable for achieving and growing a seven-figure annual contributed-revenue goal. The CDO will personally cultivate and close major gifts; lead individual, institutional, and grassroots fundraising; equip the CEO and Board as fundraising partners; and build the team and infrastructure needed for success. We are seeking an expert fundraising leader with an entrepreneurial spirit—someone who is ready to build, bring new ideas to life, and create something exceptional and enduring for At The Well.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Fundraising leadership & strategy

Develop, own, and execute a comprehensive annual and multi-year fundraising strategy with clear revenue goals, action plans, timelines, and measures of success.
Build a diversified contributed-revenue model across major gifts, individual giving, institutional funding, grassroots and digital campaigns, and other appropriate channels.
Develop revenue forecasts, pipeline projections, metrics, and reporting that identify risks and opportunities, inform organizational budgeting, and provide the CEO, COO, and Board with clear analysis of fundraising performance.
Represent At The Well at select public events, donor gatherings, conferences, and speaking engagements.

Individual giving & major gifts

Personally build and manage a portfolio of major donors and prospects, developing and executing individualized qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for each relationship.
Identify, research, cultivate, solicit, and close major gifts, with demonstrated focus on developing a pipeline of future opportunities.
Serve as the principal strategist for At The Well’s highest-priority donor relationships, overseeing moves management and equipping the CEO and Board with prospect strategy, meeting preparation, introductions, cultivation plans, solicitation support, and timely follow-up.
Provide high-touch, donor-centered stewardship that deepens relationships, supports retention and upgrades, and connects donors meaningfully to At The Well’s mission and impact.
Lead prospect research and qualification, using iWave and other tools strategically to identify and prioritize new opportunities.
Develop and implement grassroots and digital fundraising strategies in partnership with marketing and communications staff, analyzing results and adapting approaches to strengthen acquisition, retention, and the major-donor pipeline.

Institutional giving & grants

Own At The Well’s institutional fundraising strategy and grants pipeline, including funder identification, relationship development, opportunity positioning, proposal priorities, renewals, reporting, and stewardship.
Manage a grant writer or other institutional-giving support, establishing priorities, timelines, standards, and accountability while retaining executive ownership of funder relationships and results.
Coordinate proposal and report development across the organization, personally shaping, editing, or drafting high-priority and time-sensitive materials when needed.

Development communications, events, & external relationships

Develop a deep understanding of At The Well’s work and lead the creation of compelling fundraising messaging and materials, including the case for support, proposals, decks, donor reports, and campaign collateral, in partnership with the marketing and communications team.
Lead all development communications efforts, including regular donor communications as well as special grassroots fundraising campaigns,
Design and oversee fundraising and cultivation events with clear relationship and revenue objectives, integrating philanthropy thoughtfully into community and programmatic experiences.
Develop strategic relationships with donors, foundations, Jewish communal leaders, philanthropic advisors, and partner organizations that expand At The Well’s reach and funding opportunities.

Team, systems, & development operations

Recruit, manage, mentor, and develop development staff and contractors, including a development associate to manage data and CRM as well as a contract grant writer. Establish clear roles, goals, accountability, and opportunities for growth with these individuals.
Own the strategy, standards, reporting requirements, and organizational accountability for Salesforce and related development systems, partnering across the organization to ensure strong data integrity, donor documentation, gift processing, acknowledgment, reporting, and workflows.
Oversee the development budget
and make disciplined recommendations about investments in staff, technology, research, events, consultants, and donor engagement.

Executive leadership

At The Well’s Chiefs are more than functional leaders; they share responsibility for the strength, sustainability, and long-term success of the organization. This role requires someone who can hold a strategic vision while remaining deeply engaged in the work required to bring it to life. The CEO, COO, and CDO will work as a closely aligned executive team, with each leader holding clear ownership of their area while collaborating across functions to advance the organization as a whole.
Hold primary executive accountability for At The Well’s contributed-revenue performance
while remaining willing to do the hands-on work required to achieve results. We are a small team that both strategizes and executes. 
Lead with initiative and an organization-wide perspective
, understanding how development connects to programs, operations, culture, finances, communications, and mission.
Partner closely with the CEO and COO
on organizational strategy, planning, resource allocation, risk management, culture, and At The Well’s long-term health.

HOW SUCCESS WILL BE MEASURED

The CDO’s performance will be assessed through both fundraising results and the long-term strength of the development function. Core measures will include:
Annual contributed revenue raised against goal and progress toward multi-year growth targets.
Strength, value, diversification, and movement of the donor and funder pipeline, including major-gift solicitations and gifts closed.
Donor acquisition, retention, renewal, reactivation, and upgrade results.
Institutional-giving outcomes and the accuracy and usefulness of revenue forecasts, dashboards, CRM records, and reporting.
Effectiveness of the CEO, Board, staff, systems, and development team as coordinated and sustainable fundraising resources.

QUALIFICATIONS

7+ years of progressively responsible nonprofit fundraising experience, including leadership of a comprehensive development function and experience operating as a senior organizational leader.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing successful annual and multi-year strategies across multiple contributed-revenue channels, with a track record of personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing multiple six-figure gifts; experience developing or closing seven-figure opportunities is strongly preferred.
Experience building and managing a qualified major-donor portfolio, using disciplined moves management, and partnering with a CEO, senior leaders, and Board members to advance donor relationships and build an organization-wide culture of philanthropy.
Strong financial literacy, including experience with revenue forecasting, pipeline analysis, budgeting, performance metrics, and reporting.

Overview

The Director of Development & Alumni Affairs reports to the Dean of David Geffen School of Drama/Yale Repertory Theatre (DGSD/YRT). Working closely with the DGSD/YRT Associate Dean/Managing Director, the Director leads and supervises the Development and Alumni Affairs Office, overseeing annual fundraising, alumni communications, and related organizational efforts and events that support a dynamic, mission-driven operation for DGSD/YRT.

The Director is instrumental in cultivating and sustaining meaningful relationships with DGSD/YRT alumni, donors, friends, and prospects; overseeing volunteer initiatives; and meeting annual fundraising goals while delivering exceptional stewardship experiences that deepen donor and alumni commitment. The role includes planning and executing monthly, quarterly, and annual messaging; producing program- and constituency-specific communications (including newsletters); and reporting on fundraising trends and opportunities. The position requires availability for occasional travel and evening/weekend events. It also includes mentoring DGSD students in professional work assignments in the Development Department and potentially teaching workshops/courses in DGSD’s Theater Management Program.

Essential Duties

Lead all fundraising strategy and execution for DGSD/YRT, aligning solicitation campaigns and alumni affairs priorities with school and university objectives.
Design, implement, and manage comprehensive fundraising programs, including annual giving, major gifts, endowment, planned giving, and capital campaigns, in partnership with DGSD/YRT leadership and the Yale University Development Office.
Direct the full donor/prospect lifecycle: identification, research, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, proposal development, closure, stewardship, and follow-up; oversee accurate tracking and monitoring of donors and prospects.
Set and manage measurable fundraising performance targets: revenue, participation, activity.

Build and sustain strong alumni engagement and relationships; review donor profiles to identify and strategically solicit top annual donors.

Serve as liaison to the Yale University Development Office and relevant university officers/departments; collaborate closely with faculty, staff, students, and campus partners on fundraising initiatives.
Develop and manage the Development/Alumni Affairs budget; ensure effective resource allocation in support of strategic goals.
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing development team; establish a culture of responsiveness, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Supervise and mentor student rotations within the Development Office; coordinate with the Chair of the Theater Management Program to implement and evaluate student development training.
Participate in annual and long-range planning processes; contribute to short- and long-term fundraising strategy development with senior management.
Travel as required to support donor engagement and fundraising activity, consistent with Yale fundraising expectations.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Experience and proficiency in fundraising strategy, campaign planning, and execution (annual giving, major gifts, endowment, planned giving, capital campaigns) as well as prospect research, qualification/rating, portfolio management, and proposal/grant writing.
